   INTERVENOR, SLOAN SISTERS HOMESTEAD, LP’S RESPONSE TO ONCOR
  ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES
  CORPORATION’S OBJECTIONS TO, AND MOTION TO STRIKE, INTERVENOR
                           TESTIMONY

       COMES NOW, Intervenor, Sloan Sisters Homestead, LP (“Sloan Sisters”), and timely files

this Response to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation’s Objections to, and Motion to Strike, Intervenor Testimony, filed May 18, 2026,

Interchange Item No. 4726, and in support thereof respectfully shows:

                                      INTRODUCTION

       1.      For the reasons stated herein, Sloan Sisters respectfully requests that the

Administrative Law Judges overrule each of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA

Transmission Services Corporation’s (“Applicants”) objections to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9,

and deny Applicants’ request to strike Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9. Applicants’ Objections to,

and Motion to Strike, Intervenor Testimony (“Motion”) fails to properly object to Sloan Sisters’

exhibits 4 to 9. Further, Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 each fall within an exception to the rule

against hearsay and do not constitute “impermissible expert testimony.” Finally, Sloan Sisters’

exhibits 4 to 9 are each admissible under Texas Rule of Evidence 107.

                                ARGUMENTS AND AUTHORITIES

A.      Applicants have failed to specifically object to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits.

        2.      “Evidentiary objections must be timely, specific, and afford the trial court an

opportunity to cure the alleged error, if any.” 1 “The Texas Rules of Evidence require the ALJs to

rule on the specific admissibility of individual testimony and exhibits as they are offered, not in

sweeping classifications.” 2

        3.      Applicants fail to specifically object to any of Sloan Sisters’ exhibits. 3 Instead,

Applicants make generalized, global objections regarding hearsay, relevance, and non-expert

opinions in the body of the Motion. 4 Applicants’ generalized, global objections are meant to apply

to all cited testimony and exhibits listed in Exhibit A to their Motion. 5 Applicants provide only a

list of Sloan Sisters’ exhibits to which they object, with “[Hearsay; Non-Expert Opinion]”

appearing after the list of exhibits. 6 Applicants do not specify which objection applies to which

exhibit. 7 Applicants do not show how their generalized arguments regarding hearsay apply to any

of Sloan Sisters’ exhibits. 8 Applicants do not show how any of Sloan Sisters’ exhibits constitute

opinions provided by a non-expert. 9

        4.      Applicants’ generalized, global objections to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits do not meet

the required standards under the Texas Rules of Evidence. 10 Therefore, all of Applicants’

 objections to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits must be overruled. 11

B.      Even if Applicants had properly objected to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits, each of Sloan Sisters’
        exhibits are admissible.

        5.      Without waiving the above argument, should the Administrative Law Judges find

that Applicants’ objections meet the specificity requirements under the Texas Rules of Evidence,

Sloan Sisters will show that each of Applicants’ objections are without merit and must be

overruled.

        6.      In their Motion, Applicants object to the following exhibits attached to Sloan

Sisters’ testimony:

        •    Exhibit 4 – Letter from LUAS regarding archeological sites on tracts 4650, 4651, 4653,
             4655;
        •    Exhibit 5 – C.V. of Charles Hixon, Director, Llano Uplift Archeological Society;
        •    Exhibit 6 – Topographical Map of Archeological Situses on SSH, LP and Baker
             properties;
        •    Exhibit 7 – Baker Site Archeological Abstract 1;
        •    Exhibit 8 – Analysis of Aboriginal Ceramic Vessel Sherds from Baker Site; and
        •    Exhibit 9 – Abstract of Archeological Plant Remains from Baker Site. 12

Each of these exhibits fall within an exception to the rule against hearsay. Further, none of these

exhibits constitute “impermissible expert testimony.”

        i.      Hearsay

        7.      Hearsay is “a statement that: (1) the declarant does not make while testifying at the

current trial or hearing; and (2) a party offers in evidence to prove the truth of the matter asserted

in the statement.” 13

        8.      Under the Texas Rules of Evidence, testimony regarding “[a] reputation in a

community—arising before the controversy—concerning boundaries of land in the community or

 customs that affect the land, or concerning general historical events important to that community,

state, or nation” is not excluded by the rule against hearsay, regardless of whether the declarant is

available as a witness. 14

        9.       Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 each address and relate to archeological sites located

on Sloan Sisters’ property and in the area of Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and K8. 15 First,

exhibits 4 to 9 do not fall within the definition of hearsay. Exhibits 4 to 9 are not offered to prove

the truth of the matter asserted therein. Instead, exhibits 4 to 9 are merely provided to assert Keith

Bessent’s personal knowledge that an archeological group is working on Sloan Sisters’ property

and the neighbor property. 16

        10.      Even if exhibits 4 to 9 were within the definition of hearsay, each would fall under

the Reputation Concerning Boundaries or General History exception to the rule against hearsay

under Texas Rule of Evidence 803(20). Applicants acknowledge these archeological sites in their

application. 17 Archeology, by its definition,18 speaks directly to important historical events in a

community. Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 each address historical context and reputation of Sloan

Sisters’ property and the area of Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and K8. 19 Therefore, Sloan

Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 fall within the Reputation Concerning Boundaries or General History

exception to the rule against hearsay under Rule 803(20) and are admissible. Applicants’ hearsay

objections to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 must be overruled.

        11.      Because Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 each fall within the Reputation Concerning

Boundaries or General History exception to the rule against hearsay under Texas Rule of Evidence

803(20) and are admissible, Applicants’ hearsay objections to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 must

be overruled.

       ii.      Non-Expert Opinion

       12.      In their Motion, Applicants make a generalized, global objection that multiple

intervenors’ Direct Testimony and attachments “constitute impermissible expert testimony by an

unqualified witness.” 20 Applicants state “[g]enerally, the witnesses are providing opinions

concerning technical matters such as the potential health effects of electric and magnetic fields,

wildlife biology, ecology, hydrology, property valuation and appraisals, electric engineering,

power flow dynamics, or legal requirements.” 21 Applicants do not specifically state which of Sloan

Sisters’ exhibits they believe constitute impermissible expert testimony or what expert opinions

Sloan Sisters is attempting to improperly make. 22 Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 each relate to

archaeology and historical information, 23 neither of which is a category in Applicants’ list of

impermissible opinions. 24 Regardless, Sloan Sisters does not attempt to provide expert opinions

concerning the matters contained in exhibits 4 to 9. Instead, Sloan Sisters is merely testifying to

Sloan Sisters’ personal knowledge regarding the existence of archeological and historical sites

located on Sloan Sisters’ property and in the area of Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and K8.25

       13.      Because Sloan Sisters has not offered any “impermissible expert testimony”

through its exhibits 4 to 9, Applicants’ non-expert opinion objections to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4

 to 9, must be overruled.

C.      Sloan Sisters’ exhibits are admissible under Texas Rule of Evidence 107.

        14.     Under Texas Rule of Evidence 107, “[i]f a party introduces part of an act,

declaration, conversation, writing, or recorded statement, an adverse party may inquire into any

other part on the same subject. An adverse party may also introduce any other act, declaration,

conversation, writing, or recorded statement that is necessary to explain or allow the trier of fact

to fully understand the part offered by the opponent.”

        15.     In their application, under “Cultural Resource Sites within 1,000 Feet of the

Alternative Route Links,” Applicants acknowledged that archeological sites 41SS86, 41SS87,

41SS192, 41SS196, and 41SS199 are within 1,000 feet of Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and

K8. 26 These are the same archaeological sites referenced in Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9. 27 Under

Texas Rule of Evidence 107, because Applicants introduced these archaeological sites, as cultural

resources within 1,000 feet of links V2, U9, and K8, Sloan Sisters is entitled to introduce writings

and recorded statements that are necessary to explain or allow the trier of fact to fully understand

the part offered by Applicants, i.e. the cultural importance of the archeological sites and their

relevant location to links V2, U9, and K8. Therefore, Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 are admissible

under Rule 107.

                                             CONCLUSION

        16.     As shown herein, Applicants’ objections to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9, are

improper as they lack the specificity required under the Texas Rules of Evidence. This alone is

enough for the Administrative Law Judges to overrule each of Applicants’ objections. However,

 even if Applicants had properly objected, Applicants’ objections lack merit, as each of Sloan

Sisters’ objected-to exhibits fall within an exception to the rule against hearsay and do not

constitute “impermissible expert testimony.” Further, Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 are each

admissible under Rule 107. Therefore, each of Applicants’ objections to Sloan Sisters’ exhibits

must be overruled and Applicants’ request to strike Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9 must be denied.

respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges enter an order overruling all of

Sloan Sisters’ exhibits 4 to 9, and for such further relief to which Sloan Sisters may be entitled.

relevant location to links V2, U9, and K8. Therefore, Sloan Sisters' exhibits 4 to 9 are admissible

under Rule 107.
